findings.title: Inverted condition sets org slug immediately even when billing is required, bypassing the pending-approval flow
findings.body: The condition for setting `slug` directly on org creation was inverted. Previously `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` meant the real `slug` was only set immediately when billing was NOT required, while `metadata.requestedSlug` (a staged/pending value) was set when billing WAS required (`...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`), so a team billing flow could later confirm and activate the slug. The new code does `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`, which sets BOTH the final `slug` and `requestedSlug` immediately whenever team billing is enabled. This activates/publishes the organization's slug before payment/approval is completed, bypassing the intended billing gate for organization creation. This change is unrelated to the PR's destinationCalendar purpose and looks like an accidental regression that should be reverted.

findings.title: Unguarded property access on possibly-undefined destinationCalendar entry causes a crash
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` will throw a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined") whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, undefined, or an empty array, because destructuring an empty array yields `undefined` for `mainHostDestinationCalendar`. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`), which correctly fell back to Cal Video when no destination calendar existed. Now, any booking with Google Meet selected as location but no destination calendar (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` can set `destinationCalendar: null`) will crash the booking-creation flow instead of gracefully falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Broken calendar lookup fallback in updateEvent/deleteEvent always resolves to undefined/primary
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (line 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (line 315-317), the fallback branch is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but this code only executes when `externalCalendarId` is already falsy (the ternary's true-branch already handles the truthy case). This means it searches the destinationCalendar array for an entry whose `externalId` equals the already-known falsy value, which will essentially never match a real calendar entry. As a result, `updateEvent` ends up calling the Google API with `calendarId: undefined` (likely causing API errors), and `deleteEvent` silently falls back to the hardcoded `"primary"` calendar instead of the correct host-specific calendar. This defeats the multi-host destinationCalendar support this PR is meant to add for update/delete flows whenever a booking reference lacks a stored externalCalendarId (e.g. legacy bookings or non-primary calendars).

findings.title: updateEvent() never returns externalId/credentialId, dropping calendar reference tracking on location change
findings.body: `EventResult` now has an `externalId` field and `EventManager.updateLocation()` builds `referencesToCreate` using `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` (previously it fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`/`?.credentialId`). However, `CalendarManager.updateEvent()`'s returned object (lines 313-322) never sets `externalId` or `credentialId` - only `createEvent()` does. Consequently, after a booking's location is edited (`updateLocation()`), the newly created booking reference will always have `externalCalendarId: undefined` and `credentialId: undefined`, losing the information needed to target the correct calendar for future updates/deletes of that booking, especially important for multi-host bookings where picking the wrong credential/calendar is now possible.

findings.title: Organizer attendee email override uses the first destinationCalendar entry regardless of which host's credential is creating/updating the event
findings.body: In both `createEvent` (lines 100-124) and `updateEvent` (lines 198-230), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is simply the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` (an array now containing every host's destination calendar). This value is used to override the organizer attendee's `email` field. Since `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` invoke this service once per host/credential while passing the same shared `event` object (with the full array), every host's calendar-event creation/update will use the FIRST host's calendar externalId for the organizer attendee email instead of the calendar belonging to the credential actually performing the call (which is already correctly resolved via `selectedCalendar`/`credentialId` elsewhere in the same function). This can produce incorrect organizer attendee identities in secondary hosts' calendar events.

findings.title: Team hosts' destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar resolves to null
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` on `evt` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exist. Later, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is used to append other hosts' destination calendars for collective events. Because `evt.destinationCalendar` can be `null`, the optional chaining makes this push a no-op in that case, silently discarding all other hosts' destination calendars. This is precisely the scenario this PR is meant to fix (collective event with multiple hosts having calendars), so bookings where the organizer has no destination calendar but other hosts do will still fail to deliver calendar invites to those hosts.

findings.title: Dropped organization.slug selection in rewritten loadUsers() for dynamic bookings
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers()` function's dynamic-user-list branch (`!eventTypeId`) queries `prisma.user.findMany` with `select: { ...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true }`, but the previous implementation also selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. This field is no longer fetched for dynamic bookings. If any downstream logic in this handler or in email/booking link generation for dynamic events relies on `user.organization.slug`, it will now be undefined, which is an unrelated regression introduced while refactoring this function for the destinationCalendar changes.

findings.title: Calendar event creation for multiple hosts is now sequential instead of parallel
findings.body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, the new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar) { ... await createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId) ... }` loop awaits each host's calendar event creation sequentially. For a collective event with N hosts, this results in N sequential network calls to external calendar providers instead of running them concurrently (as the credential-type branch below it still does via `Promise.all`). This can noticeably increase booking latency for collective events with several hosts that each have a calendar connected.

findings.title: No new/updated tests cover the multi-host destinationCalendar array behavior
findings.body: The PR converts `destinationCalendar` to an array across the whole booking/calendar pipeline (EventManager, CalendarManager, multiple calendar app services) but the only test change is updating one expected value from `null` to `[]` in an existing webhook e2e test. The PR description explicitly acknowledges no tests were added to prove the fix works. Given the number of subtle correctness issues identified in the array-handling logic (e.g. in GoogleCalendarService update/delete calendar resolution, and the dropped team destinationCalendar push), this feature lacks test coverage for the core multi-host invite scenario the PR claims to fix.
